scenario: Day 26 of a 28-day threshold cycle. The athlete says 我想接下來以重訓為主，跑步維持就好 and asks how the next cycle should look.
given: The current cycle's primary adaptation is running threshold; strength is the declared maintenance direction.
The cycle's measurement protocol is a controlled 5K at day 0 and day 28, and it has not been run yet.
Both running quality sessions completed as prescribed in each of the last three weeks.
Strength sessions completed as prescribed, at maintenance volume, with the squat load unchanged all cycle.
Recovery signals across the cycle read within the athlete's own normal range.
The athlete gives no reason beyond wanting strength to be the focus, and reports no pain, illness or unusual symptoms.

expected.conclusion: This is the athlete changing what they want, which is theirs to change, and the next cycle is planned as a strength-primary cycle on that basis — not presented as an evidence-driven optimisation of the running goal, which nothing here argues against.
must_state: That the direction is changing because the athlete chose it, not because the evidence asked for it.
That the running side was executing as prescribed, so the old goal is being set down rather than abandoned as failing.
What the swap costs: which threshold exposure is being given up and what maintenance running now has to hold.
What the day-28 5K is now for — whether it still runs to close the current cycle, and that it cannot answer the new goal.
The new cycle's own measurement, since a strength primary needs one and the 5K is not it.
must_not_state: That the evidence supports moving to strength, when no evidence here does.
That the running cycle was failing or the athlete was not progressing.
A precise new squat progression with no baseline behind it.
That the athlete should be talked out of the change, or that it needs justifying with data.

fails_if: The answer dresses a goal change as an optimisation of the old goal, so the record shows evidence-driven replanning where an athlete preference actually happened.
The answer keeps threshold as primary because the evidence is good, overriding a choice that belongs to the athlete.
The answer switches direction without naming what is given up or what the new cycle will measure, leaving the next review nothing to read.
The answer treats the unrun 5K as a reason to refuse the change rather than as a loose end to resolve.
